subject.title: Cron session accumulation can silently exhaust agent context window — no guardrails or warnings

question: Should this issue remain the umbrella until both high-frequency cron warnings and cron-session retention cleanup are resolved, or should maintainers split the remaining guardrails into narrower canonical issues now?
rationale: The source-backed gaps are real, but the warning threshold and base-session cleanup semantics affect operator noise and persisted session state, so automation should not choose the permanent product boundary alone.

options.title: Keep Umbrella Until Slices Resolve
options.body: Use this issue to track the overall cron/session guardrail problem while reviewing the open warning and retention candidates, then split only any leftovers.

options.title: Split Remaining Guardrails
options.body: Confirm narrower canonical issues for context-threshold warnings and cleanup behavior, then let each PR close only its own slice.

options.title: Reject Fixed Warning Threshold
options.body: If maintainers do not want a hard-coded sub-30-minute advisory, close or narrow the warning PR and keep retention cleanup as the primary bug path.

recommendation.title: Keep Umbrella Until Slices Resolve
recommendation.body: Use this issue to track the overall cron/session guardrail problem while reviewing the open warning and retention candidates, then split only any leftovers.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved decision centers on the cron/session lifecycle and pruning contract this history most directly ties to.
